outside_input_curated_positive_audit.quote: On June 4, 2026, the Energy Department celebrated Antares Nuclear’s advanced reactor, Mark-0, successfully reaching criticality through a test demonstration at INL. This achievement was the first time in over 40 years that a new privately developed non-light-water nuclear reactor reached criticality in America. The zero-power fueled criticality demonstration confirmed the reactor would be able to operate safely and established a baseline for allowing subsequent reactors to produce electricity in 2027 and the following years.
outside_input_curated_positive_audit.meaning: Reached zero-power test criticality; not commercial production.

outside_input_curated_positive_audit.quote: On June 18, 2026, the Energy Department announced Valar Atomics’ advanced test reactor, Ward 250, successfully reached criticality at the Utah San Rafael Energy Lab in Emery County, Utah.
outside_input_curated_positive_audit.meaning: Advanced test reactor criticality; 250 is part of the model name, not units.

outside_input_curated_positive_audit.quote: On June 30, 2026, Deployable Energy’s Unity completed a criticality demonstration, also hosted at INL—marking the third reactor to reach criticality ahead of the July 4 deadline.
outside_input_curated_positive_audit.meaning: Completed a criticality test, not delivery or qualified commercial production.

outside_input_curated_positive_audit.quote: On July 4, 2026, Aalo Atomics’ test reactor, Aalo-X, completed a zero-power fueled criticality demonstration at INL, marking the fourth reactor to reach the Energy Department’s criticality milestone.
outside_input_curated_positive_audit.meaning: Zero-power criticality test, not qualified commercial production.

outside_input_curated_positive_audit.quote: Thanks to the Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF), bolstered by the Working Families Tax Cut, the Energy Department is bringing previously shuttered nuclear power plants back online, and financing the development of new nuclear projects in the United States. On June 23, 2026, the Energy Department announced financing for long-lead time supply chain items to accelerate the timeline for the deployment of 10 new large-scale commercial nuclear reactors. The Energy Department is supporting the restart of previously shut-down nuclear power plants; including, Palisades 800 MW nuclear generating station in Michigan, and the Crane Restart project—an 835 MW nuclear plant in Pennsylvania. More restarts are expected to be announced in the future. In March 2026, the Energy Department’s Office of Nuclear Energy (in collaboration with EDF) launched the Utility Power Reactor Incremental Scaling Effort (UPRISE) initiative to accelerate domestic nuclear energy production. UPRISE aims to add 2.5 GW of nuclear capacity by 2027, and 5 GW by 2029—the equivalent of five new nuclear reactor years sooner than any other nuclear technology.
outside_input_curated_positive_audit.meaning: Restart project nameplate rating, not added operating capacity.
